text:
Pactrun 1.0.0-alpha.7
Usage:
  pactrun [--format human|json|jsonl] <command> [options]

Manage installed Packs, long-lived Instances and Pack-defined operations.

pack
  Install Packs or generate a Package ID.

pack generate-id
pactrun pack generate-id
  Generate a new Package ID without opening managed storage.

pack install
pactrun pack install <directory-or-pack-file> [--package-name <name>] [--revision-name <name>] [--metadata-conflict overwrite|keep]
  Validate and install immutable Pack content; does not start a service.
Options:
  --package-name <name>
    Assign a local Package name on installation; does not silently rename an existing object.
  --revision-name <name>
    Assign a local Revision name on installation; conflicts leave no partial installation.
  --metadata-conflict <overwrite|keep>
    Explicitly choose overwrite or keep for imported metadata conflicts.
Examples:
  pactrun pack install ./example.pack --package-name app --revision-name initial

package
  Manage local Package names.

package rename
pactrun package rename <package> <name>
  Set or change a local Package name without changing identity.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

package unname
pactrun package unname <package>
  Remove a local name; does not delete the Package or its Revisions.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision
  Inspect, name, export or delete installed Revisions.

revision list
pactrun revision list [--limit <1..500>] [--after <cursor>] [--no-trunc]
  List Revisions newest-installed first; copy the returned cursor to continue.
Options:
  --limit <count>
    Bound and continue a listing using its returned cursor.
  --after <cursor>
    Bound and continue a listing using its returned cursor.
  --no-trunc
    Show complete identifiers instead of shortened human display IDs.
  Object IDs accept unique lowercase hexadecimal prefixes of at least eight digits. --no-trunc shows full identifiers; pagination cursors are not object references.
Examples:
  pactrun revision list --limit 10

revision show
pactrun revision show <revision-reference>
  Inspect an installed Revision and its public declarations.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision metadata
  Inspect Revision descriptions and provenance.

revision metadata show
pactrun revision metadata show <revision-reference>
  Inspect presentation and local metadata for a Revision.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision rename
pactrun revision rename <package>:<revision> <name>
  Set or change a local Revision name within its Package.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision unname
pactrun revision unname <package>:<revision>
  Remove a local name; does not delete the Revision or rebind Instances.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision export
pactrun revision export <revision-reference> --output <base-path> [--include-portable-metadata]
  Export an installed Revision as a portable .pack archive.
Options:
  --output <base-path>
    Publish a new bundle, appending the command's .pack or .snapshot suffix.
  --include-portable-metadata
    Include eligible portable metadata, not local notes or trust labels.
  Always appends .pack: rv -> rv.pack; rv.pack -> rv.pack.pack.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision note
  Manage a local Revision note.

revision note show
pactrun revision note show <revision-reference>
  Read a Revision local note.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision note set
pactrun revision note set <revision-reference> --value <text> (--expect-absent | --expect <text>)
  Set a local note with an explicit expected previous value.
Options:
  --value <text>
    Supply metadata and an exact compare-and-set expectation.
  --expect-absent
    Supply metadata and an exact compare-and-set expectation.
  --expect <previous-value>
    Supply metadata and an exact compare-and-set expectation.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision note clear
pactrun revision note clear <revision-reference> (--expect-absent | --expect <text>)
  Clear a local note with an explicit expected previous value.
Options:
  --expect-absent
    Supply metadata and an exact compare-and-set expectation.
  --expect <previous-value>
    Supply metadata and an exact compare-and-set expectation.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision trust
  Manage a local descriptive trust assessment.

revision trust show
pactrun revision trust show <revision-reference>
  Inspect the local trust label; it is not publisher authentication.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision trust set
pactrun revision trust set <revision-reference> <trusted|distrusted> (--expect-absent | --expect <trusted|distrusted>)
  Set a local trust label with an explicit expected previous value.
Options:
  --expect-absent
    Supply metadata and an exact compare-and-set expectation.
  --expect <previous-value>
    Supply metadata and an exact compare-and-set expectation.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision trust clear
pactrun revision trust clear <revision-reference> (--expect-absent | --expect <trusted|distrusted>)
  Clear a local trust label with an explicit expected previous value.
Options:
  --expect-absent
    Supply metadata and an exact compare-and-set expectation.
  --expect <previous-value>
    Supply metadata and an exact compare-and-set expectation.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

revision delete
pactrun revision delete <revision-reference>
  Delete an eligible unreferenced Revision.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

instance
  Create, inspect and manage Instances.

instance create
pactrun instance create <name> --revision <reference> [--input-file <id>=<path>]... [--input-stdin <id>]
  Create a managed Instance from an installed Revision and optional initial Inputs.
pactrun instance create <name> --revision <reference> --restore-from <snapshot-id> [restore-execution-options]
  Create an Instance and execute the declared restore capability from a Snapshot.
Options:
  --revision <revision-reference>
    Select an installed Revision by a unique package:revision reference.
  --input-file <id=path>
    Supply a new Instance Input from the indicated file.
  --input-stdin <input-id>
    Supply a new Instance Input from standard input.
  --restore-from <snapshot-id>
    Create the Instance, then restore this Snapshot. Failure can leave a created Instance; inspect the result.
  --param <id=value>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --param-file <id=path>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --param-stdin <id>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --authorize-recovery-override
    Bypass only the initial guard; does not repair or acknowledge recovery.
  --startup-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --execution-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --termination-grace-ms <milliseconds>
    Set the termination grace period; the default is 5000ms.
  --no-retain-hook-text
    Do not retain Hook free text; live output remains enabled.
  --cancel-on-output-close
    For JSONL execution only, request cancellation when the receiver closes stdout.
  Restore execution options require --restore-from and exclude --plan. Initial Input options cannot be combined with Restore.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.
Examples:
  pactrun instance create demo --revision app:initial

instance list
pactrun instance list
  List currently managed Instances.

instance show
pactrun instance show <instance>
  Inspect current Revision, readiness, bindings and recovery guard.

instance migration-paths
pactrun instance migration-paths <instance> --to <reference> [--limit <1..100>] [--after <path-id>] [--no-trunc]
  List declared migration routes without acquiring files or observing services.
Options:
  --to <revision-reference>
    Choose the target Revision and an explicit declared migration route.
  --limit <count>
    Bound and continue a listing using its returned cursor.
  --after <cursor>
    Bound and continue a listing using its returned cursor.
  --no-trunc
    Show complete identifiers instead of shortened human display IDs.
  Object IDs accept unique lowercase hexadecimal prefixes of at least eight digits. --no-trunc shows full identifiers; pagination cursors are not object references.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.

instance migrate
pactrun instance migrate <instance> --to <reference> [--plan] [--path <path-id>] [--input-file <target-digest>/<input-id>=<path>]... [--param <target-digest>/<parameter-id>=<value>]... [--param-file <target-digest>/<parameter-id>=<path>]... [--param-stdin <target-digest>/<parameter-id>] [--authorize-declassification] [--authorize-recovery-override] [--startup-timeout-ms <ms>] [--execution-timeout-ms <ms>] [--termination-grace-ms <ms>]
  Migrate along the selected declared path; --plan only previews the operation.
Options:
  --to <revision-reference>
    Choose the target Revision and an explicit declared migration route.
  --plan
    Preview without execution; Migration previews do not acquire operator files or observe services.
  --path <path-id>
    Choose the target Revision and an explicit declared migration route.
  --input-file <target-digest/input-id=path>
    Supply a declared Input for a specific target Revision on the selected path.
  --param <target-digest/id=value>
    Supply a typed parameter for one exact edge of the selected Migration path.
  --param-file <target-digest/id=path>
    Supply a typed parameter for one exact edge of the selected Migration path.
  --param-stdin <target-digest/id>
    Supply a typed parameter for one exact edge of the selected Migration path.
  --authorize-declassification
    Allow only declared Secret declassification on the selected path.
  --authorize-recovery-override
    Bypass only the initial guard; does not repair or acknowledge recovery.
  --startup-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --execution-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --termination-grace-ms <milliseconds>
    Set the termination grace period; the default is 5000ms.
  --no-retain-hook-text
    Do not retain Hook free text; live output remains enabled.
  --cancel-on-output-close
    For JSONL execution only, request cancellation when the receiver closes stdout.
  Revision references use package:revision, with local names or IDs. Local names are case-sensitive and contain 1 to 31 ASCII characters.
  Input files are target-qualified and acquired before execution. --plan does not acquire Input files or observe live services; it reads parameter sources to validate the entire selected path.
  Same-name parameters on different edges are independent. At most one parameter may read stdin; paths with interactive Hooks cannot use parameter stdin.

instance delete
pactrun instance delete <instance> [--plan] [--if-version <token>] [--param <id>=<value>]... [--param-file <id>=<path>]... [--param-stdin <id>] [execution-options]
  Run declared Cleanup and reclaim owned service storage; irreversible.
Options:
  --plan
    Preview without execution; Migration previews do not acquire operator files or observe services.
  --if-version <token>
    Require the exact observed state token; stale state is refused.
  --authorize-recovery-override
    Bypass only the initial guard; does not repair or acknowledge recovery.
  --startup-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --execution-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --termination-grace-ms <milliseconds>
    Set the termination grace period; the default is 5000ms.
  --no-retain-hook-text
    Do not retain Hook free text; live output remains enabled.
  --cancel-on-output-close
    For JSONL execution only, request cancellation when the receiver closes stdout.
  --param <id=value>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --param-file <id=path>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --param-stdin <id>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  State-version tokens require their complete values, not ID prefixes.
  Operation-scoped Cleanup accepts its declared parameters. Each new execution supplies them again or uses defaults; finalization-only does not execute the Hook or accept parameters.

instance abandon
pactrun instance abandon <instance> [--plan] [--if-version <token>]
  End management and retain remaining service data; does not stop the service.
Options:
  --plan
    Preview without execution; Migration previews do not acquire operator files or observe services.
  --if-version <token>
    Require the exact observed state token; stale state is refused.
  --authorize-recovery-override
    Bypass only the initial guard; does not repair or acknowledge recovery.
  --startup-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --execution-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --termination-grace-ms <milliseconds>
    Set the termination grace period; the default is 5000ms.
  --no-retain-hook-text
    Do not retain Hook free text; live output remains enabled.
  --cancel-on-output-close
    For JSONL execution only, request cancellation when the receiver closes stdout.
  State-version tokens require their complete values, not ID prefixes.
  Abandon does not run Cleanup and accepts no Hook parameters.

instance history
  Inspect retained Instance identities.

instance history list
pactrun instance history list [--limit <1..500>] [--after <instance-id>] [--no-trunc]
  List live and retired Instance identities.
Options:
  --limit <count>
    Bound and continue a listing using its returned cursor.
  --after <cursor>
    Bound and continue a listing using its returned cursor.
  --no-trunc
    Show complete identifiers instead of shortened human display IDs.
  Object IDs accept unique lowercase hexadecimal prefixes of at least eight digits. --no-trunc shows full identifiers; pagination cursors are not object references.

instance history show
pactrun instance history show <instance-id>
  Inspect historical Instance facts without rebinding its former name.

instance deletion
  Inspect deletion attempts and confirm externally completed Cleanup.

instance deletion list
pactrun instance deletion list [--limit <1..500>] [--after <instance-id>] [--no-trunc]
  List retained deletion attempts and retirement facts.
Options:
  --limit <count>
    Bound and continue a listing using its returned cursor.
  --after <cursor>
    Bound and continue a listing using its returned cursor.
  --no-trunc
    Show complete identifiers instead of shortened human display IDs.
  Object IDs accept unique lowercase hexadecimal prefixes of at least eight digits. --no-trunc shows full identifiers; pagination cursors are not object references.

instance deletion show
pactrun instance deletion show <instance-id>
  Inspect the retained deletion attempt and remaining obligations by Instance ID.

instance deletion confirm-complete
pactrun instance deletion confirm-complete <instance-id> --attempt <run-id> --if-version <token> --assert-cleanup-complete
  Assert externally verified Cleanup completion for the exact attempt.
Options:
  --attempt <run-id>
    Identify the attempt and assert externally verified Cleanup.
  --if-version <token>
    Require the exact observed state token; stale state is refused.
  --assert-cleanup-complete
    Identify the attempt and assert externally verified Cleanup.
  State-version tokens require their complete values, not ID prefixes.

instance resolve-manual-recovery
pactrun instance resolve-manual-recovery <instance> [--if-version <token>]
  Acknowledge externally verified recovery; does not itself repair the service.
Options:
  --if-version <token>
    Require the exact observed state token; stale state is refused.
  State-version tokens require their complete values, not ID prefixes.

input
  Manage Instance Inputs and Secrets.

input list
pactrun input list <instance>
  List active and retained Input bindings without exporting their values.

input set
pactrun input set <instance> <input-id> (--file <path> | --stdin) [--if-version <token>]
  Acquire and bind supplied bytes; this does not deploy or restart a service.
Options:
  --file <path>
    Read Input bytes from this file.
  --stdin
    Read Input bytes from standard input.
  --if-version <token>
    Require the exact observed state token; stale state is refused.
  State-version tokens require their complete values, not ID prefixes.
Examples:
  pactrun input set demo config --file ./config.json

input export
pactrun input export <instance> <input-id> --output <path|-> [--authorize-secret-export]
  Export a binding to a new file or stdout; Secret export requires authorization.
Options:
  --output <path|->
    Write binding bytes to a new file, or use - for raw standard output.
  --authorize-secret-export
    Explicitly authorize protected export.

input delete
pactrun input delete <instance> <input-id> [--if-version <token>]
  Remove the selected Input binding; does not delete service-owned data.
Options:
  --if-version <token>
    Require the exact observed state token; stale state is refused.
  State-version tokens require their complete values, not ID prefixes.

action
  Inspect Pack-defined Actions and parameters.

action list
pactrun action list <instance>
  List the Actions declared by the active Revision.

action show
pactrun action show <instance> <action>
  Inspect an Action declaration, parameters and execution requirements.

invoke
pactrun invoke <instance> <action> [options]
  Execute a declared Action, or preview it with --plan.
Options:
  --param <id=value>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --param-file <id=path>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --param-stdin <id>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --plan
    Preview without execution; Migration previews do not acquire operator files or observe services.
  --authorize-recovery-override
    Bypass only the initial guard; does not repair or acknowledge recovery.
  --startup-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --action-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Bound Action execution (unlimited when omitted); other operations use --execution-timeout-ms.
  --termination-grace-ms <milliseconds>
    Set the termination grace period; the default is 5000ms.
  --no-retain-hook-text
    Do not retain Hook free text; live output remains enabled.
  --cancel-on-output-close
    For JSONL execution only, request cancellation when the receiver closes stdout.
Examples:
  pactrun action show demo inspect
  pactrun invoke demo inspect --plan

run
  Inspect and manage retained Run history.

run list
pactrun run list [<instance> | --instance-id <id>] [--limit <1..500>] [--after <run-id>] [--no-trunc]
  List Run history for all Instances or a selected exact Instance.
Options:
  --instance-id <instance-id>
    Select retained history by exact Instance identity rather than its current name.
  --limit <count>
    Bound and continue a listing using its returned cursor.
  --after <cursor>
    Bound and continue a listing using its returned cursor.
  --no-trunc
    Show complete identifiers instead of shortened human display IDs.
  Object IDs accept unique lowercase hexadecimal prefixes of at least eight digits. --no-trunc shows full identifiers; pagination cursors are not object references.

run show
pactrun run show <run-id>
  Inspect a Run outcome, failure, progress and current recovery guard.

run reconcile
pactrun run reconcile
  Terminalize confirmed lost owners without replaying Hooks.

run artifact
  Export or delete retained Run Artifacts.

run artifact export
pactrun run artifact export <run-id> <output-id> --output <path> --authorize-sensitive-export [--edge <source-digest>/<target-digest>]
  Export a retained Run Artifact with explicit sensitive-export authorization.
Options:
  --output <path>
    Write to a new file; existing destinations are not replaced.
  --authorize-sensitive-export
    Explicitly authorize protected export.
  --edge <source-digest/target-digest>
    Select one exact Migration edge from the retained Run path; required for edge-scoped reports.
  Edge prefixes resolve against this Run, even after Revision removal. Same-name reports on other edges are not a fallback. Scoped results require machine interface 1.0-alpha.4.

run artifact delete
pactrun run artifact delete <run-id> <output-id> [--edge <source-digest>/<target-digest>]
  Delete the selected retained Run Artifact.
Options:
  --edge <source-digest/target-digest>
    Select one exact Migration edge from the retained Run path; required for edge-scoped reports.
  Edge prefixes resolve against this Run, even after Revision removal. Same-name reports on other edges are not a fallback. Scoped results require machine interface 1.0-alpha.4.

run delete
pactrun run delete <run-id> [--delete-artifacts]
  Delete eligible Run history; associated artifacts need explicit deletion intent.
Options:
  --delete-artifacts
    Include associated Artifacts when deleting eligible Run history.

snapshot
  Capture, restore and manage Snapshots.

snapshot list
pactrun snapshot list [--instance <instance>] [--no-trunc]
  List Snapshots, optionally filtered by Instance.
Options:
  --instance <instance>
    Filter by the selected live Instance.
  --no-trunc
    Show complete identifiers instead of shortened human display IDs.
  Object IDs accept unique lowercase hexadecimal prefixes of at least eight digits. --no-trunc shows full identifiers; pagination cursors are not object references.

snapshot show
pactrun snapshot show <snapshot-id>
  Inspect Snapshot identity and recorded metadata.

snapshot capture
pactrun snapshot capture <instance> [execution-options]
  Execute the Pack-defined capture capability to create a Snapshot.
Options:
  --param <id=value>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --param-file <id=path>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --param-stdin <id>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --plan
    Preview without execution; Migration previews do not acquire operator files or observe services.
  --authorize-recovery-override
    Bypass only the initial guard; does not repair or acknowledge recovery.
  --startup-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --execution-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --termination-grace-ms <milliseconds>
    Set the termination grace period; the default is 5000ms.
  --no-retain-hook-text
    Do not retain Hook free text; live output remains enabled.
  --cancel-on-output-close
    For JSONL execution only, request cancellation when the receiver closes stdout.

snapshot restore
pactrun snapshot restore <instance> <snapshot-id> [execution-options]
  Execute the Pack-defined restore capability against a selected Snapshot.
Options:
  --param <id=value>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --param-file <id=path>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --param-stdin <id>
    Supply declared typed parameters from one chosen source.
  --plan
    Preview without execution; Migration previews do not acquire operator files or observe services.
  --authorize-recovery-override
    Bypass only the initial guard; does not repair or acknowledge recovery.
  --startup-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --execution-timeout-ms <milliseconds>
    Set invocation deadlines; omitted values are unlimited.
  --termination-grace-ms <milliseconds>
    Set the termination grace period; the default is 5000ms.
  --no-retain-hook-text
    Do not retain Hook free text; live output remains enabled.
  --cancel-on-output-close
    For JSONL execution only, request cancellation when the receiver closes stdout.

snapshot verify
pactrun snapshot verify <snapshot-id>
  Check the selected Snapshot against its integrity contract.

snapshot import
pactrun snapshot import <bundle-path>
  Validate and import a Snapshot bundle; does not restore a service.

snapshot export
pactrun snapshot export <snapshot-id> --output <base-path> --authorize-sensitive-export
  Export a Snapshot bundle with explicit sensitive-export authorization.
Options:
  --output <base-path>
    Publish a new bundle, appending the command's .pack or .snapshot suffix.
  --authorize-sensitive-export
    Explicitly authorize protected export.
  Always appends .snapshot: backup -> backup.snapshot; backup.snapshot -> backup.snapshot.snapshot.

snapshot delete
pactrun snapshot delete <snapshot-id>
  Delete an eligible Snapshot.

service-storage
  Inspect service storage and detached allocations.

service-storage list
pactrun service-storage list <instance> [--retained]
  List declared service storage bindings; include retained bindings with --retained.
Options:
  --retained
    Include or select retained bindings rather than only active bindings.

service-storage detached
  Inspect or explicitly discard detached allocations.

service-storage detached list
pactrun service-storage detached list [--no-trunc]
  List allocations retained after Instance management ended.
Options:
  --no-trunc
    Show complete identifiers instead of shortened human display IDs.
  Object IDs accept unique lowercase hexadecimal prefixes of at least eight digits. --no-trunc shows full identifiers; pagination cursors are not object references.

service-storage detached show
pactrun service-storage detached show <allocation-id> [--reveal-location]
  Inspect a detached allocation; reveal native locations only when requested.
Options:
  --reveal-location
    Explicitly request native location disclosure and access intent.

service-storage detached discard
pactrun service-storage detached discard <allocation-id> --confirm-discard
  Irreversibly reclaim the selected detached allocation with explicit consent.
Options:
  --confirm-discard
    Explicitly authorize irreversible detached-allocation disposal.

resource
  Inspect and locate declared service resources.

resource list
pactrun resource list <instance> [--retained]
  List declared service resource associations.
Options:
  --retained
    Include or select retained bindings rather than only active bindings.

resource show
pactrun resource show <instance> <resource-id> [--retained]
  Inspect a resource association without observing the live service.
Options:
  --retained
    Include or select retained bindings rather than only active bindings.

resource observe
pactrun resource observe <instance> <resource-id> [--retained]
  Observe the selected live resource without changing the service.
Options:
  --retained
    Include or select retained bindings rather than only active bindings.

resource locate
pactrun resource locate <instance> <resource-id> --intent <read|write> [--retained]
  Request an explicitly read- or write-intended native resource location.
Options:
  --intent <read|write>
    Explicitly request native location disclosure and access intent.
  --retained
    Include or select retained bindings rather than only active bindings.

storage
  Inspect and collect unreferenced stored content.

storage gc
pactrun storage gc [--plan]
  Collect eligible unreferenced managed content; --plan only previews collection.
Options:
  --plan
    Preview without execution; Migration previews do not acquire operator files or observe services.

hook
  Access helpers for an active Shell Loader Session.
  Help does not require a Session. Executing helpers requires an active Shell Loader Session.

hook session
pactrun hook session [--output <path>]
  Inspect the active Shell Loader Session.
Options:
  --output <path>
    Write to a new file; existing destinations are not replaced.
  Execution requires an active Shell Loader Session. Helper payloads use the helper interface, not the global --format renderer.
  Result files must be new. --output cannot be combined with byte-copy options; registration and receipts are not durable Run success.

hook parameter
pactrun hook parameter <id> [--output <path>]
  Read a declared typed parameter as a JSON value.
Options:
  --output <path>
    Write to a new file; existing destinations are not replaced.
  Execution requires an active Shell Loader Session. Helper payloads use the helper interface, not the global --format renderer.
